summary: Sony's rhythm-strategy series about commanding Patapons with drum patterns, with modern remasters and rereleases changing the best-play routes for the first two games and Patapon 3.

entries.title: Patapon

emulation.emulator: Native PC; PPSSPP for PSP original
emulation.notes: Use Steam Replay for main capture and PPSSPP only for original-version comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Modern PC release with 60 fps-oriented requirements; PS4 Remastered offers official 4K output on compatible displays.

primary.why: PATAPON 1+2 REPLAY is the newest official remaster route for the first game, adding support features such as difficulty settings, timing adjustment, and persistent command display; the PC release is the most capture-friendly primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play PATAPON 1+2 REPLAY on Steam for the main run. Use Nintendo Switch only for its local co-op feature, and PS4 Remastered or PSP only for historical comparison.

secondary.exclusive_content: PATAPON 1+2 REPLAY has 1-4 player local co-op as a Nintendo Switch-only feature.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Switch version's local co-op mode if multiplayer coverage matters.
secondary.why: 1-4 player local co-op is Nintendo Switch-only.

all_releases.reason: skip: historically first, but lower-fidelity and less accessible than modern remasters.

all_releases.fidelity: Patapon Remastered with 1080p and 4K output on compatible displays.
all_releases.reason: skip: strong fidelity route, but the 2025 Replay version adds newer support features.

all_releases.fidelity: PATAPON 1+2 REPLAY remaster with Switch-only local co-op.
all_releases.reason: secondary: same modern bundle, but the Switch version uniquely has 1-4 player local co-op.
skip: modern console route, but PC is the preferred capture platform and Switch has the exclusive local co-op feature.

all_releases.fidelity: PATAPON 1+2 REPLAY Steam release with modern support features.
all_releases.reason: primary: newest official remaster route and best capture workflow.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC Replay is the best main-run route, while Nintendo Switch uniquely has local co-op.

entries.remaster_caveats: PS4 Remastered has official 1080p/4K output; Replay is newer and adds support features, while Switch gets the local co-op feature.

entries.title: Patapon 3

emulation.emulator: Native PS5 digital PSP conversion; PPSSPP for PSP original
emulation.notes: Use PS5 for main capture and PPSSPP/PSP only for original multiplayer behavior.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS5 output of the converted PSP release with up-rendering and filters.

primary.why: The PS4/PS5 digital release is the current official route and adds up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters; PS5 is the preferred modern console target.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS5 digital release for the main run. Use original PSP hardware or PPSSPP only for original multiplayer/peripheral-dependent behavior that the PS4/PS5 conversion may not support.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original PSP multiplayer/peripheral behavior may not be fully supported by the PS4/PS5 conversion.
secondary.what_to_play: Use PSP hardware or PPSSPP to verify original multiplayer behavior if covering Patapon 3's multiplayer-focused design.
secondary.why: Patapon 3 supports single-player and multiplayer, while the converted release does not support PSP peripherals and some functionality may be unavailable.

all_releases.reason: secondary: lower fidelity, but preserves original PSP-era multiplayer/peripheral behavior.

all_releases.fidelity: Digital PSP conversion with up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters.
all_releases.reason: skip: same conversion family as PS5; PS5 is the preferred modern console target.

all_releases.fidelity: Digital PSP conversion with up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters.
all_releases.reason: primary: current official high-fidelity route for the final Patapon entry.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The PS5 conversion has modern rendering/features, but the original PSP route remains the secondary check for multiplayer/peripheral-dependent behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a PSP conversion with added features, not a full remaster, and PSP peripheral functionality is unsupported.
